report.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (cvxpy at commit `8fb412018aef`), the test fails: `q` is computed incorrectly (k-th smallest threshold) and `t` is only nonzero on top-k indices, so either the `assert q.value == pytest.approx(8.0)` fails and/or the feasibility check `assert np.all(x.value <= t.value + q.value + 1e-10)` fails for middle elements (6.0 and 8.0 in the provided vector). On the fixed revision (the commit after PR #3220), `q` is computed as the k-th largest threshold (= 8.0 for the given x and k=2) and `t` is initialized for all elements as `max(0, x-q)`, so both `q/t` assertions and the feasibility inequalities pass.

examples.expected_output: Warm-start produces `q = 8.0` (k-th largest threshold) and `t = max(0, x-q)` for all elements, so `x <= t+q` holds for all i.
examples.buggy_output_reported: Warm-start produces an incorrect `q` computed from the k-th smallest and initializes `t` only for top-k indices, making `x_i <= t_i + q` violated for middle elements (notably indices with values 6.0 and 8.0).

comparison.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (cvxpy at commit `8fb412018aef`), the test fails: `q` is computed incorrectly (k-th smallest threshold) and `t` is only nonzero on top-k indices, so either the `assert q.value == pytest.approx(8.0)` fails and/or the feasibility check `assert np.all(x.value <= t.value + q.value + 1e-10)` fails for middle elements (6.0 and 8.0 in the provided vector). On the fixed revision (the commit after PR #3220), `q` is computed as the k-th largest threshold (= 8.0 for the given x and k=2) and `t` is initialized for all elements as `max(0, x-q)`, so both `q/t` assertions and the feasibility inequalities pass.
